newsitem.title: UK: Merrill Lynch decides on new London HQ.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch decides on new London HQ.

text.p: U.S. investment banking giant Merrill Lynch on Tuesday confirmed it had decided to build a new European headquarters on the site of a post office in King Edward Street near St Paul's Cathedral in the City of London.
"Merrill Lynch intends to use the site for construction of a new headquarters for its operations in Europe, the Middle East and Africa," the firm said in a statement.

Merrill said it had reached agreement, subject to receiving the appropriate approvals, to buy the Post Office site, which would give it space to house up to 5,500 staff in London and allow it to expand from its current level of 4,000 employees.

The site currently houses a former Royal Mail sorting office and the existing Post Office Counters Ltd headquarters. Merrill said it plans to rebuild on the sorting office site but retain the listed post office headquarters building as an adjoining site.
"This investment in a new headquarters facility underscores the depth of our commitment to the entire region and to the City of London as a major financial centre," Merrill said.

The firm said it would ensure the construction was in keeping with the historic character of the surroundings. It expects the development to be completed by mid-2001. It will retain its existing Farringdon Road building, which houses 1,000 staff and also its Chester Street office in the west of London with 400 people in its international private client group.
Merrill will leave its main Ropemaker Street office by mid-2001.

There had been suggestions Merrill would move to the Docklands area to the east of the City -- London's traditional financial heartland, but bankers said senior Merrill executives had looked at this option but decided to stay in the City.
